---
title: "Compare fitted models"
description: "Use T2 for nested homogeneous fits and information criteria for likelihood comparisons."
---

Use `angular_lrtest()` for nested homogeneous models fitted to the same
observations with the same reference direction and sign. The example
generates independent von Mises errors around a known mean direction.

```{r}
library(CircularRegression)

set.seed(481)
n <- 120
d <- data.frame(ref = runif(n, -pi, pi), x = runif(n, -pi, pi))
mu <- atan2(sin(d$ref) + 0.3 * sin(d$x), cos(d$ref) + 0.3 * cos(d$x))
d$y <- mu + as.numeric(circular::rvonmises(n, circular::circular(0), kappa = 4))

reduced <- angular(y ~ ref, d, reference = "first")
full <- angular(y ~ ref + x, d, reference = "first")
angular_lrtest(full, reduced)
```

For a comparison of probability models, fit them to the same response
rows and check that both fits converged. Here the homogeneous model uses
a common concentration and the consensus model uses observation-specific
concentrations.

```{r}
varying <- consensus(y ~ ref + x, d)
c(homogeneous = full$fit_status, consensus = varying$fit_status)
AIC(full, varying)
BIC(full, varying)
```
